correctness.rationale: Every original table is uniquely reconstructed from two labelled equality partitions and a row/column-distinct quotient of the same rank. Every rank-d quotient has exactly |GL(d,q)| full-rank basis factorizations. Row-distinctness/column-distinctness are equivalent to injective vector tuples in the respective factors, and subspace-lattice Möbius inversion gives their exact spanning counts T_q. This proves the full formula, support and EGF. The standalone verifier independently exhausts every binary table through 4x4, every ternary table through 2x2, verifies support through d=5 and rank-normalization for q=2,3 and sizes through 6. Numerical tests are not substituted for the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: A simultaneous finite-field rank and row/column-clarification joint distribution was not found in the checked related research and mathematical databases. The inspected prior definitions, unranked exact tables, real/nonnegative rank census, and special graph-rank theorems have strictly different quantifiers or invariants; neither a simple known table nor an accessible stronger theorem was identified that subsumes the full claim. Ordinary factorization, Stirling numbers and subspace Möbius inversion are acknowledged as existing tools. Residual risk is earlier equivalent enumeration under alternative vocabulary.
residual_risks: An undiscovered rank-refined formula for twin-free bipartite adjacency matrices, or an equivalent finite-field matrix enumeration in coding or design theory, might subsume the new statement.
The inspected exact tables are unranked, but mathematical search cannot establish uniqueness of the novel joint statistic.

value.rationale: Equality-based clarification is the standard canonical simplification of formal incidence contexts, and binary rank is an intrinsic algebraic invariant unchanged by deleting repeated rows and columns. The theorem gives the full exact joint probability law for these independent context parameters for every size, an exact sharp rank-feasibility boundary, a trivariate EGF, and normalization against two known marginal theories. These results motivate comparison of observed contexts against random incidence null models; no unspecified downstream theorem is needed for the intrinsic full-family enumeration.
